_source: Which Census block equivalency file each state votes on in a cycle. Maps: U.S. Census Bureau Redistricting Data Office 119th- and 120th-Congress block equivalency files (https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/decennial/rdo/mapping-files/). Legal status per state (source: the official page of each act or order, verified 2026-10-13): each state's enacting act or order (reasons below), cross-checked against Wikipedia's '2025–2026 United States redistricting' (read 2026-09-28); each official state block file available (TX, CA, FL, NC, OH) matches the Census CD120 file exactly. A hand-maintained record of legal facts (AGENTS.md 3a); edit it when a state's map or its legal status changes, then rerun backend/scripts/build_county_district_crosswalk.py and build_district_topology.py.
_use: One list, three readers: build_county_district_crosswalk.py and build_district_topology.py (which lines a state's counties and outlines come from), and live_results/sync.redrawn_states (which also drives the elections API's newDistrictLines, its cross-district incumbent match and the results payload's redrawnStates; a House seat in a state voting on a map other than the one its members were elected on — those going into the election, or the sitting Congress — has no knowable holder going into the election — the district of the same number is a different district — so no flip is announced against the old district's member; a cycle not listed keeps the newest earlier cycle's maps). A state never listed votes on its CD119 lines, and the crosswalk script refuses to build if its CD119 and CD120 blocks differ. Also read by app/redistricting.py, which cites each entry's `source` (title, issuing body, official URL) on the redistricting pages. Each entry's `kind` says how the map in force was set (act: enacted by the legislature; ballot_measure: approved by voters; commission: adopted by a redistricting commission; court_order: set or held by a court) and `settled` the day the reason names that settled it for the cycle (the act signed, the vote, the order); app/redistricting.watch reads both for the redistricting watch.
